Assume the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth
tangent-bundle conventions. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth
Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with metric-selected
connection $\nabla$ and inverse metric $g^{ab}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open,
let $\psi\in C^\infty(U,\mathbb R)$ be a real scalar field, and let $X$ be a
smooth vector field on $U$. Define the wave operator
$\Box_g\psi:=g^{ab}\nabla_a\nabla_b\psi$ and the symmetric covariant tensor

$$Q_{ab}[\psi]:=(\nabla_a\psi)(\nabla_b\psi)-\frac12 g_{ab}g^{cd}(\nabla_c\psi)(\nabla_d\psi).$$

Define the multiplier covector by $J^X_a[\psi]:=Q_{ab}[\psi]X^b$. The
associated energy-current vector is $j_X^a[\psi]:=-g^{ab}J^X_b[\psi]$; this
sign convention makes its flux through a future spacelike slice equal to the
density $Q_{ab}n^aX^b$ when $n$ is the future unit normal. The test-wave
equation is $\Box_g\psi=0$ on $U$. These objects are defined on the fixed
background $g$; $Q$ is not automatically an SI matter stress-energy tensor,
is not inserted into an Einstein equation here, and does not evolve $g$.

If $\psi$ is dimensionless and the coordinates have length units, the
components of $Q$ have units of inverse length squared. This dimensional fact
does not identify $Q$ with a physical stress tensor without an independently
specified field normalization and coupling.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field
on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **Lie
derivative of the metric along $\xi$**, written $\mathcal L_\xi g$, is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field obtained by the flow definition of
[[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]] applied to $g$: for the local flow
$\Phi_t$ of $\xi$,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g:=\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g .$$

The field $\xi$ is a **Killing field** of $(M,g)$ (an **isometry generator**,
or a **Killing vector**) when

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0 .$$

The equivalent local characterization

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0,$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and
$\xi_b:=g_{bc}\xi^c$ is the lowered field, is proved in
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a); the definition
itself asserts neither direction. Whether a given metric has Killing fields is
a property of that metric: neither existence nor uniqueness of a Killing field
is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field
$\xi=0$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]).

**(a) Characterization of Killing fields.** For every smooth vector field
$\xi$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), with
$\xi_b=g_{bc}\xi^c$ the lowered field,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0 .$$

**(b) Contraction along geodesics.** If $\xi$ is a Killing field and
$\gamma:I\to M$ is a geodesic with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its affine parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]), then $t\mapsto
g_{\gamma(t)}(\xi_{\gamma(t)},\gamma'(t))$ is constant on $I$.

**(c) Conserved current.** Let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $T$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $\xi$ be a Killing field on $U$. Then
$J^{a}:=T^{ab}\xi_b$ is a smooth vector field on $U$ with
$\nabla_aJ^a=0$; consequently the flux balance of
[[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] clause (b) applies to $J$
on every smooth singular $4$-chain contained in $U$.

**(d) On-shell conservation of the Hilbert tensor.** Let $c>0$, let
$S:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be a model action with Hilbert stress-energy tensor
$T$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]). For the flow diffeomorphisms $F$
below, suppose the configuration set $\mathcal X$ carries specified maps
$P_F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$ with $P_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$; write
$F^*\varphi:=P_F(\varphi)$. For geometric matter fields these are the
model's pullbacks; no pullback operation on an arbitrary set is implicit.
For **every** smooth compactly supported vector field $\xi$, its flow
$\Phi_v$ is global
([[def-complete-vector-field]], [[def-local-and-global-flow]]); this holds for
every compactly supported smooth field, using the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] through
[[thm-compactly-supported-vector-fields-are-complete]]. Write
$G(u,v):=S(\Phi_v^*g,\Phi_u^*\varphi)$ for the simultaneous pullback by the
flow (this presupposes that the pairs lie in $\mathcal D$, which is part of the
hypotheses below). Suppose (H1)–(H4) hold for **every** such $\xi$ (with
its own $G$ and parameter neighborhood):

- **(H1)** the map $G$ is defined on a neighborhood of $(0,0)$ in
  $\mathbb R^2$ and is differentiable at $(0,0)$;
- **(H2)** $\partial_uG(0,0)=0$ (the matter configuration $\varphi$ satisfies
  its model equations in this direction);
- **(H3)** $\partial_vG(0,0)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_MT_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$,
  where $q^{ab}:=\partial_v(\Phi_v^*g)^{ab}|_{v=0}$ (the metric variation is
  represented by the Hilbert tensor);
- **(H4)** $G(s,s)=S(g,\varphi)$ whenever $(s,s)$ lies in that neighborhood
  (invariance of the action under simultaneous pullback by the flow).

Then $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $M$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(a) Observers.** An **observer at $p$** is a tangent vector
$n\in T_pM$ such that $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ is future-directed in the sense of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], that is, $g_p(n,N_p)<0$. Because
$g_p(n,n)=-1\neq0$, an observer is timelike and in particular nonzero
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Observers at $p$ exist:
the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and
$n:=N_p/\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}$ satisfies $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and
$g_p(n,N_p)=-\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}<0$, where the square root is the
nonnegative root of [[def-rational-power]]; then $-n$ is a unit timelike
vector with $g_p(-n,N_p)>0$, so it is not an observer, and the two vectors
$n,-n$ point in opposite time directions.

**(b) Rest space.** For an observer $n$ at $p$, the **rest space** of $n$ is
the $g_p$-orthogonal complement of the line $\mathbb Rn$,

$$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM: g_p(v,n)=0\},$$

in the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. It is
a linear subspace of $T_pM$. The further facts that $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and
that the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive definite are proved
in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]; they are consequences, not
part of the definition.

**(c) Spatial projection.** The **spatial projection** of the observer $n$ is
the map

$$h_n:T_pM\longrightarrow T_pM,\qquad h_n(v):=v+g_p(n,v)\,n .$$

The map is linear because $g_p$ is bilinear, its image is contained in
$n^{\perp}$, and it fixes $n^{\perp}$ pointwise; that it is the
$g_p$-orthogonal projection onto $n^{\perp}$ with kernel $\mathbb Rn$ is
proved in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]].

**(d) Scope.** An observer at $p$ is a single tangent vector. It is not an
ordered basis or frame of $T_pM$, not a chart, not a field of observers such as
the congruences defined later on this page, and not a curve or a worldline: no
parametrized curve, clock reading, proper time or measurement is attached to
$n$ by this definition. The physical reading of an observer as the direction
of an ideal clock's worldline, and the measurement interpretation of the
observer-relative quantities introduced later on this page, belong to the
physical postulates and unit conventions of the framework and are not asserted
here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $h:=h_n$,
$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,n)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and
$\mathbb Rn=\{\lambda n:\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$. Then:

1. $h:T_pM\to T_pM$ is linear, $h(n)=0$, $h(v)=v$ for every $v\in n^{\perp}$
   and $h\circ h=h$; its kernel is $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$, its image is
   $\operatorname{im}h=n^{\perp}$, and
   $T_pM=\mathbb Rn\oplus n^{\perp}$ is an orthogonal direct sum: every
   $v\in T_pM$ has the unique decomposition

   $$v=-g_p(v,n)\,n+h(v),$$

   in which $-g_p(v,n)n\in\mathbb Rn$ and $h(v)\in n^{\perp}$.
2. For all $v,w\in T_pM$ the **projection identity**

   $$g_p(h(v),h(w))=g_p(v,w)+g_p(v,n)g_p(n,w)$$

   holds; in particular $g_p(h(v),h(v))=g_p(v,v)+g_p(v,n)^2$.
3. $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
   definite.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with associated quadratic form
$q(v)=\eta(v,v)$. A vector $v\in V$ is

- **timelike** when $q(v)<0$;
- **null**, or **lightlike**, when $v\neq 0$ and $q(v)=0$;
- **spacelike** when $q(v)>0$;
- **causal** when it is timelike or null.

The zero vector $0\in V$ satisfies $q(0)=0$ and is consequently **none** of
timelike, null or spacelike: the null case explicitly excludes it, and the
timelike and spacelike cases exclude it by $q(0)=0$ together with the strict
inequalities. The **causal character** of a nonzero vector $v$ is the sign of
the real number $q(v)$, and the three names are attached to the three signs as
above. When no confusion arises, the pairing $\eta$ itself is written
$\langle v,w\rangle:=\eta(v,w)$.

**Each nonzero vector has exactly one causal character.** For a nonzero
$v\in V$ the real number $q(v)$ satisfies exactly one of $q(v)<0$, $q(v)=0$,
$q(v)>0$ by trichotomy of the order on $\mathbb R$, so $v$ is timelike, null or
spacelike, and no two of the three alternatives can hold at once. The causal
vectors are therefore exactly the nonzero vectors that are timelike or null,
and the zero vector is causal in no sense introduced here.

For vectors $u,v$ in a real or complex inner product space,

$$|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\lVert u\rVert\lVert v\rVert.$$

Equality holds if and only if $u$ and $v$ are linearly dependent, including the case in which either vector is zero.

Set $\ell=\sharp_g(d\psi)$ and $a=g(\ell,n)$. Then
$b=h_n(\ell)=\ell+a n$, so $\ell=b-a n$ and $g(b,n)=0$ by [F2]–[F3]. It follows that $g^{-1}(d\psi,d\psi)=g(\ell,\ell)=-a^2+|b|^2$. Substitution into [F1], using $g(n,n)=-1$, gives $Q(n,n)=a^2-\tfrac12(-a^2+|b|^2)=\tfrac12(a^2+|b|^2)$.
Let $\alpha:=-g(n,X)$ and $Y:=X-\alpha n$. Future causality in [F4] gives $\alpha\geq0$; [F2] gives $Y=h_n(X)\in n^\perp$. Since $g(X,X)=-\alpha^2+|Y|^2\leq0$, one has $|Y|\leq\alpha$.

By [F1] and step 1.1,
$Q(n,X)=\alpha a^2+a\,g(b,Y)+\tfrac{\alpha}{2}(-a^2+|b|^2)=\tfrac{\alpha}{2}(a^2+|b|^2)+a\,g(b,Y)$.

Apply [F5] and $|Y|\leq\alpha$ from step 1.2:
$Q(n,X)\geq\tfrac{\alpha}{2}(a^2+|b|^2)-\alpha|a||b|=\tfrac{\alpha}{2}(|a|-|b|)^2\geq0$. If $\alpha=0$, step 1.2 gives $Y=0$ and hence $X=0$, for which $Q(n,X)=0$ as well. This proves the causal flux inequality, including the null case.

is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field
$\xi=0$.

This item assumes the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through
the tangent-bundle structure used by
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c)
([[def-countable-choice]]); no further choice principle is used.

**(a) Parameters and the Schwarzschild radius.** Let $c>0$ and $G_N>0$ be real
constants and let $m_*>0$ be a real **mass parameter**. Put

$$s:=\frac{2G_Nm_*}{c^2}>0 .$$

The number $s$ is the **Schwarzschild radius** of the datum. Neither $c$,
$G_N$ nor $m_*$ is measured here; the physical reading of $c$ and $G_N$ as the
framework's conversion and Newton constants and of $m_*$ as a mass is fixed by
the physical conventions of the framework, not by this definition.

**(b) The underlying manifold and its product charts.** Let $S^2:=S_2(0,1)=
\{y\in\mathbb R^3:\lVert y\rVert_2=1\}$ be the unit Euclidean sphere with the
subspace topology of [[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]. Specify its
smooth structure as the maximal atlas generated by the following two charts
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). For $\varepsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$ put
$p_\varepsilon=(0,0,\varepsilon)$ and
$U_\varepsilon=S^2\setminus\{p_\varepsilon\}$, and define

$$\sigma_\varepsilon:U_\varepsilon\to\mathbb R^2,\qquad \sigma_\varepsilon(y)=\frac{(y_1,y_2)}{1-\varepsilon y_3}.$$

These open domains cover $S^2$. Each chart is a homeomorphism onto
$\mathbb R^2$, with inverse, for $u=(u_1,u_2)$ and $q=u_1^2+u_2^2$,

$$\sigma_\varepsilon^{-1}(u)=\left(\frac{2u_1}{1+q},\frac{2u_2}{1+q},\varepsilon\frac{q-1}{1+q}\right).$$

The two inverse identities follow by substitution; all displayed denominators
are nonzero on their domains. On the overlap both transition maps are
$u\mapsto u/(u_1^2+u_2^2)$ on $\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}$, hence smooth.
The subspace is Hausdorff and has a countable basis given by intersections
with Euclidean balls of rational centres and positive rational radii.
Thus these charts specify a smooth two-manifold without boundary. This is
the standard sphere structure used for the round metric below: the inclusion
has the displayed smooth local parametrizations, and their differentials
are injective because composition with $\sigma_\varepsilon$ is the identity.
Let $M$ be the product manifold

$$M:=\mathbb R\times(s,\infty)\times S^2$$

with the product smooth structure
([[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]]);
it is a smooth four-manifold without boundary. Write $x^0:M\to\mathbb R$ and
$r:M\to(s,\infty)$ for the first and second projections and $\iota:M\to S^2$
for the third. A **product chart** of $M$ is a smooth chart on the product
whose angular part is a smooth chart of $S^2$. In a **spherical-polar product
chart**, $0<\vartheta<\pi$ and the components of the round metric
$\gamma_{S^2}$ of [[ex-the-round-metric-on-the-sphere-as-an-induced-metric]]
are $\gamma_{22}=1$, $\gamma_{23}=\gamma_{32}=0$,
$\gamma_{33}=\sin^2\vartheta$. These polar charts omit the two poles; ordinary
smooth sphere charts around the poles complete the product atlas.

**(c) The metric.** Let $f:(s,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be the smooth function

$$f(r):=1-\frac{s}{r} .$$

Define $g$ globally by the coordinate-free expression

$$g=-f\,d(x^0)\otimes d(x^0)+f^{-1}\,dr\otimes dr+r^2\,\iota^*\gamma_{S^2}.$$

In every spherical-polar product chart its component functions are

$$g_{00}:=-f(r),\qquad g_{11}:=\frac{1}{f(r)},\qquad g_{22}:=r^2,\qquad g_{33}:=r^2\sin^2\vartheta,$$

and $g_{ab}:=0$ whenever $a\ne b$, $a,b\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, with the index order
$(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$. This is a smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field on all of $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]); the component display is local
to spherical-polar charts, and $f>0$ because $r>s$. The pair $(M,g)$ is the **Schwarzschild exterior
metric of mass parameter $m_*$**; the datum of this definition is the
quadruple $(c,G_N,m_*,g)$. With these parameters fixed, write $(M,g,N)$
for its associated geometric datum, with $N$ as in clause (d). The geometric
datum depends on the parameters only through $s$ and does not retain $c$,
$G_N$ and $m_*$ separately. That $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ is not asserted here; it is proved in the companion metric-properties lemma of this page (its
justification record in the frontmatter), which also records the equivalent
coordinate-free description
$g=-f\,d(x^0)\otimes d(x^0)+f^{-1}\,dr\otimes dr+r^2\,\iota^*\gamma_{S^2}$.

**(d) Time orientation and the Schwarzschild chart.** The field
$N:=\partial_0$ is the smooth product vector field on $M$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); the chart components of $g$
are independent of $x^0$, so $N$ is the restriction of a global vector field,
and $g(N,N)=-f(r)<0$ at every point. The datum carries the time orientation
$N$. Spherical-polar product charts are **Schwarzschild charts** of the datum;
at the poles the same metric is represented in the smooth sphere charts of
the product atlas. We write $t$ for the coordinate $x^0/c$ when the datum is
read in the framework's unit conventions.

**(e) Scope.** The domain of the datum is the exterior region $r>s$; the
definition asserts nothing about $r=s$, about $r\le 0$, about any matter, or
about any equation satisfied by $g$. The horizon $r=s$ is not part of the
datum, and a continuation of the metric to $r=s$ requires the separate constructions recorded on this page, the
regularity lemma for the advanced chart and the Kruskal model-properties
lemma. Whether the datum is a solution of the
framework's field law is proved, not defined, in the Ricci-and-Einstein-tensor lemma of this
page.

Let $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $m_*>0$ and let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior
datum of mass parameter $m_*$ with Schwarzschild radius
$s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$ ([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]). Then:

**(a) Global metric and local components.** $M$ is a smooth four-manifold
without boundary and $g$ is the smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field
globally defined by

$$g=-f\,d(x^0)\otimes d(x^0)+f^{-1}\,dr\otimes dr+r^2\,\iota^*\gamma_{S^2}.$$

In every spherical-polar product chart $(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$ its
components are

$$g_{00}=-f(r),\qquad g_{11}=\frac{1}{f(r)},\qquad g_{22}=r^2,\qquad g_{33}=r^2\sin^2\vartheta,\qquad g_{ab}=0\ (a\ne b),$$

where $f(r)=1-s/r$, $\iota:M\to S^2$ is the third projection and
$\gamma_{S^2}$ is the round metric of the unit sphere. The component display
is local to the spherical-polar charts; the global tensor formula includes
the poles.

**(b) Lorentzian signature.** At every $p\in M$ the form $g_p$ is
nondegenerate with inertia $(3,1,0)$; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth
Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$.

**(c) Time orientation.** The global product field $N=\partial_0$ is smooth
and nowhere vanishing, and $g_p(N_p,N_p)=-f(r(p))<0$ at every $p$; it is
therefore a time orientation of $(M,g)$. The globally defined base fields
$\partial_0,\partial_r$ are orthogonal with squared norms $-f$ and $f^{-1}$.
In a spherical-polar chart the angular coordinate fields are orthogonal with
positive squared norms $r^2$ and $r^2\sin^2\vartheta$; at a pole use any
angular chart and the positive-definite round metric instead.

**(d) Domain of the coordinates.** Product charts form an atlas covering
$M$. Spherical-polar charts are defined on the regular angular locus
$0<\vartheta<\pi$ and omit the poles; pole charts are ordinary smooth charts
of $S^2$. The functions $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are smooth on $r>s$, and the
spherical-polar component functions are smooth on their chart domains.

**(e) Conventions.** The global tensor identity holds on all of $M$; the
displayed component identities are in spherical-polar product charts. In pole
charts the sphere block is $r^2$ times the round-metric component matrix.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum with Schwarzschild radius
$s>0$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]). Let
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}:=\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the product
smooth structure and let $\iota_{\mathrm{ext}}:M_{\mathrm{ext}}\to S^2$ be the
third projection. Its product atlas includes ordinary sphere charts at the
poles ([[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]]).
Define the **tortoise function**

$$r_*(r):=r+s\log\left|\frac{r}{s}-1\right|,\qquad r>0,\ r\ne s,$$

on each of the two intervals $(0,s)$ and $(s,\infty)$, and define the
**advanced-chart metric** globally on $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$ by

$$g_{\mathrm{ext}}=-f(r)\,dv\otimes dv+dv\otimes dr+dr\otimes dv+r^2\,\iota_{\mathrm{ext}}^*\gamma_{S^2}.$$

In spherical-polar product charts its components are

$$g_{\mathrm{ext}}=-f(r)\,dv^2+2\,dv\,dr+r^2\,d\Omega^2,$$

namely $g_{vv}=-f$, $g_{vr}=g_{rv}=1$,
$g_{\vartheta\vartheta}=r^2$, $g_{\varphi\varphi}=r^2\sin^2\vartheta$ and all
other components zero. In another sphere chart the angular block is
$r^2(\gamma_{ij})$. Then:

**(a) Smooth Lorentzian metric.** $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is a smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field on $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and at every point it is
nondegenerate with inertia $(3,1,0)$; hence $(M_{\mathrm{ext}},g_{\mathrm{ext}})$
is a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$r>0$, including $r=s$.

**(b) Time orientation.** The smooth vector field

$$N_{\mathrm{ext}}:=A(r)\,\partial_v-\partial_r,\qquad A(r):=\frac{f(r)+\sqrt{f(r)^2+4}}{2}>0,$$

satisfies $g_{\mathrm{ext}}(N_{\mathrm{ext}},N_{\mathrm{ext}})<0$ everywhere
and $g_{\mathrm{ext}}(N_{\mathrm{ext}},\partial_v)<0$ everywhere; hence
$N_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is a time orientation of $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and on the
region $r>s$ it determines the same future cone as the datum's time
orientation $\partial_v=\partial_0$.

**(c) Isometric embedding of the exterior.** The map
$\Phi:M\to M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, $(x^0,r,\omega)\mapsto(x^0+r_*(r),r,\omega)$
restricts to a diffeomorphism of $M$ onto the open subset $\{r>s\}$ of
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and $\Phi^*g_{\mathrm{ext}}=g$; the exterior datum is
therefore isometric to the region $r>s$ of the extension.

**(d) Vacuum and Kretschmann scalar of the extension.** The
metric-selected connection of $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ exists and is unique, its
Ricci tensor, scalar curvature and Einstein tensor vanish identically on
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and its Kretschmann scalar equals

$$R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=\frac{12s^2}{r^6}$$

on all of $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$. In particular the scalar is smooth and finite on
the horizon $r=s$, where it takes the value $12/s^4$.

**(e) The horizon is a null hypersurface.** The level set $\{r=s\}$ is a
smooth null hypersurface of $(M_{\mathrm{ext}},g_{\mathrm{ext}})$ whose null
generator direction is $\partial_v$; every smooth product-chart frame remains
a basis across $r=s$. In spherical-polar charts
$\det(g_{\mathrm{ext}})=-r^4\sin^2\vartheta$; in an arbitrary sphere chart
the determinant is $-r^4\det(\gamma_{ij})$, which is nonzero.

**(f) Scope.** The extension constructed here is a smooth Lorentzian
manifold containing the exterior isometrically and regular across $r=s$; it
is not claimed to be maximal, and no uniqueness or global structure theorem
is asserted. The region $r\le0$ and the surfaces relevant to the Kruskal
model of this page are outside this statement.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. At a point $p$ of a time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold, let $n$ be a future-directed unit timelike vector, let
$X\in T_pM$ be future causal, and let $\psi$ be a smooth real scalar. Put
$\ell:=\sharp_g(d\psi)$, $a:=d\psi(n)$,
$b:=h_n(\ell)\in n^\perp$, and $|b|^2:=g(b,b)$, where $h_n$ is the spatial
projection relative to $n$. Then

$$Q(n,n)=\frac12\bigl(a^2+|b|^2\bigr),\qquad Q(n,X)\geq0.$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $M$ carry an orientation in the
sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]] (so that its
charts that are oriented in that orientation have orientation-preserving
transition maps), and let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection. This item
fixes the metric volume form, the flux of a current through oriented $3$-faces
and finite-chain charges. The orientation of $M$ is an independent datum: it is
not determined by the metric and not by the time orientation.

**(a) Metric volume density and volume form.** Let $(U,x)$ be an oriented
chart, with metric components $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (a)). Define the **metric volume
density**

$$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}>0\qquad\text{on }U,$$

a strictly positive smooth function because $g_{ab}$ is smooth and
$g_p$ is nondegenerate. In the chart define the local $4$-form

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,U}:=w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3,$$

with the exterior product of [[def-wedge-product-of-differential-forms]] and the
coordinate covector fields of
[[prop-local-coordinate-expression-for-a-differential-form]]. That these local
forms agree on chart overlaps and therefore define one smooth nowhere-vanishing
$4$-form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ on $M$ — the **metric volume form** — is proved in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (a), together
with the reading statement of clause (b) there: in every oriented chart
$\mathrm{vol}_g=w\,dx^0\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^3$, and on every positively
oriented $g_p$-orthonormal basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $T_pM$ one has
$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=1$.

**(b) Current flux through oriented $3$-faces and chains.** Let $J$ be a
smooth vector field on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **current
$3$-form** of $J$ is the contraction

$$\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

the interior product of the $4$-form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ with $J$
([[def-interior-product-of-a-form-by-a-vector-field]]).

By a **smooth singular $k$-simplex** of $M$ — the convention of the library
definition `def-smooth-singular-simplex` (differential-geometry track),
restated here so this page is self-contained — we mean a map
$\sigma:\Delta^k\to M$ whose domain is the standard $k$-simplex
$$\Delta^k=\Bigl\{t\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:t_i\ge0,\ \textstyle\sum_it_i=1\Bigr\},$$
for which there exist an open set $O\subseteq A^k=\{t\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:\sum_it_i=1\}$
containing $\Delta^k$ and a smooth map $\bar\sigma:O\to M$ with
$\bar\sigma|_{\Delta^k}=\sigma$; the extension is not part of the simplex
data, and degenerate parametrizations are allowed. With the integration of
forms over such simplices
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]]), a **$3$-face** is
a smooth singular $3$-simplex $\sigma$, and the **flux of $J$ through
$\sigma$** is the real number

$$\Phi_J(\sigma):=\int_\sigma\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

A **finite smooth singular $k$-chain** — the convention of the library
definition `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes`, restated here —
is a finite formal real linear combination $\Sigma=\sum_i c_i\sigma_i$ of
smooth singular $k$-simplices. For such a $3$-chain the **flux of $J$ through
$\Sigma$** is defined additively,

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma):=\sum_i c_i\,\Phi_J(\sigma_i),$$

a definition independent of the written expression for $\Sigma$, because a
finite formal sum is evaluated by adding the finitely many coefficients and
inserting a zero coefficient changes nothing. $\Phi_J(\Sigma)$ is the **charge**
of the current $J$ assigned to $\Sigma$ when the model reads $J$ as a conserved
current; that reading belongs to the physical postulates and is not part of
this definition.

**(c) Non-null faces and their unit normals.** A $3$-dimensional linear subspace
$H\subseteq T_pM$ is **nondegenerate** for $g_p$ when the restriction of $g_p$
to $H$ is nondegenerate, equivalently when $H\cap H^\perp=\{0\}$ in the
orthogonality of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. A
smooth singular $3$-simplex $\sigma$ is **non-null at** a parameter point $t$
when the span of the three velocity vectors
$\sigma_*\partial_1|_t,\sigma_*\partial_2|_t,\sigma_*\partial_3|_t$ has
dimension $3$ and is nondegenerate at $\sigma(t)$, and **non-null** when this holds at every
parameter point. For a non-null face the **unit normal** $\nu$ at that point is
the unique vector of $T_{\sigma(t)}M$ with $\nu\in H^\perp$,
$g(\nu,\nu)\in\{-1,+1\}$ and $(\nu,\sigma_*\partial_1,\sigma_*\partial_2,
\sigma_*\partial_3)$ a positively oriented basis of $T_{\sigma(t)}M$; its
existence, uniqueness and its sign $\varepsilon:=g(\nu,\nu)$ are proved in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c), together
with the density identity of clause (c) used to read $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g$ on
such a face. Rank-deficient faces and rank-three faces with degenerate induced
metric are not assigned a unit normal; their flux is defined
by the $3$-form $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g$ itself, as in clause (b).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with an
orientation, metric-selected connection $\nabla$, metric volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ and current flux $\Phi_J$ as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]], and let $J$ be a smooth vector
field on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Write
$\nabla_aJ^a$ for the divergence of $J$.

**(a) Exterior derivative of the current form.** As smooth $4$-forms on $M$,

$$d\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)=\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

**(b) Flux balance (Stokes).** For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$
of $M$ — a finite formal real sum of smooth singular $4$-simplices, the
library convention `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes` restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — and the flux
$\Phi_J$ of the induced boundary $3$-chain
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]],
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]]),

$$\Phi_J(\partial C)=\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently, if $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for smooth singular $3$-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)+\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

In particular, if $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $C$ then
$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)$, and if moreover
$\Phi_J(B)=0$ then $\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)=\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)$: equal charges need a
vanishing side flux, not merely a divergence-free current.

**(c) Non-null face formula.** Let $\sigma$ be a smooth singular $3$-simplex —
a map $\sigma:\Delta^3\to M$ admitting a smooth extension to a neighbourhood
of the standard $3$-simplex inside its affine plane, the convention restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — that is
non-null at a parameter point $t$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (c)), with
$v_i:=\sigma_*\partial_i|_t$ spanning the hyperplane $H$ and with the unit
normal $\nu^{*}$ adapted to the ordered basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ as in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c); write
$\varepsilon:=g_{\sigma(t)}(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})\in\{-1,1\}$. Then

$$\sigma^{*}\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)\big|_{t} =\varepsilon\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(J,\nu^{*}\bigr)\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_{\sigma(t)}(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|} .$$

Equivalently, the tangent vector $J$ is decomposed as
$J=\varepsilon g(J,\nu^{*})\nu^{*}+w'$ with $w'\in H$, and only the normal
component contributes to the flux through the face.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.
$$\sigma^{*}\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)\big|_{t} =\varepsilon\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(J,\nu^{*}\bigr)\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_{\sigma(t)}(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|} .$$

derivations.claim: In the advanced coordinates all coefficients of $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ are independent of $v$, so the coordinate formula for $\mathcal L_{\partial_v}g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ gives $\mathcal L_Tg_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$ and $T$ is Killing by [F3]. The multiplier identity [F2] therefore gives $\nabla^aJ_a^T=0$ on $C$. Since $j_T^a=-g^{ab}J_b^T$, its divergence also vanishes.

The Statement orients each spacelike face so its adapted unit normal is the future unit normal $n_j$. By [F8] its current flux density is $-g(j_T,n_j)\,d\mu_{\Sigma_j}$. The definition $j_T^a=-g^{ab}Q_{bc}T^c$ gives $g(j_T,n_j)=-Q_{ab}n_j^aT^b$, so integration yields $\Phi_{j_T}(\Sigma_j)=\int_{\Sigma_j}Q_{ab}n_j^aT^b\,d\mu_{\Sigma_j}=E_j$.

The isometric exterior has $T$ future timelike for $r>s$, and [F5] makes $T$ future null on $\mathcal H^+$. Thus $T$ is future causal throughout the stated closure. Applying [F6] to each spacelike face gives $E_1,E_2\geq0$.

On $\mathcal H^+$, the inverse of the $(v,r)$ metric block has $g^{rv}=1$ and $g^{rr}=f=0$. Hence $j_T^r=-g^{rb}Q_{bv}=-Q_{vv}=-(T\psi)^2$, since $g_{vv}=0$ there. With
$\mathrm{vol}_{g_{\mathrm{ext}}}=r^2\,dv\wedge dr\wedge d\Omega$ and the outward boundary orientation at the inner face $r=s$, the pullback of $\iota_{j_T}\mathrm{vol}_{g_{\mathrm{ext}}}$ is $(T\psi)^2s^2\,dv\wedge d\Omega$. Therefore this face flux is exactly $F_H\geq0$.

By [F7] and step 1.1, $\Phi_{j_T}(\partial C)=0$. The stated boundary decomposition and additivity of flux give $\Phi_{j_T}(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_{j_T}(\Sigma_1)+F_H+F_{\mathrm{out}}=0$. Using step 1.2 to identify the two face fluxes with $E_2$ and $E_1$ gives the asserted balance.

On the static exterior slices $g(T,T)=-f$ and $n=f^{-1/2}T$, so $T=\sqrt f\,n$ and bilinearity gives $Q(n,T)=\sqrt f\,Q(n,n)$. By [F6] with $X=n$, $Q(n,n)\geq0$, while the coefficient $\sqrt f$ tends to zero as $r\downarrow s$. In the regular extension $g(T,T)=-f$ vanishes at $r=s$ by [F5], so $T$ becomes null there and the static Killing slice density loses its transverse coercivity.

citations.quote:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M>0$, $0<|a|<M$, and use the length
coordinates of the subextremal Kerr datum. Let $H^+$ be a regular patch of
its future horizon, let $T$ and $\Phi$ be the stationary and axial Killing
fields, and let
$\chi:=T+\Omega_H\Phi$ with
$\Omega_H:=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$ be the future null generator there. A smooth
complex scalar $u$ on a horizon patch is an $(\omega,m)$ **horizon mode**
when $\omega\in\mathbb R$, $m\in\mathbb Z$, and

$$Tu=-i\omega u,\qquad \Phi u=im u.$$

Its **shifted horizon frequency** is
$\widetilde\omega:=\omega-m\Omega_H$. By linearity of $\chi$, every such
mode satisfies $\chi u=-i\widetilde\omega u$. The parameter $\omega$ has
units reciprocal to the Kerr time coordinate, $m$ is dimensionless, and
$\Omega_H$ has the same units as $\omega$. This is a local definition of
mode data only; it does not assert that a nonzero mode extends to a global
solution of the wave equation.

Assume the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth
tangent-bundle conventions. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth
Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with metric-selected
connection $\nabla$ and inverse metric $g^{ab}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open,

associated energy-current vector is $j_X^a[\psi]:=-g^{ab}J^X_b[\psi]$; this
sign convention makes its flux through a future spacelike slice equal to the
density $Q_{ab}n^aX^b$ when $n$ is the future unit normal. The test-wave
equation is $\Box_g\psi=0$ on $U$. These objects are defined on the fixed
background $g$; $Q$ is not automatically an SI matter stress-energy tensor,
is not inserted into an Einstein equation here, and does not evolve $g$.

If $\psi$ is dimensionless and the coordinates have length units, the
components of $Q$ have units of inverse length squared. This dimensional fact
does not identify $Q$ with a physical stress tensor without an independently
specified field normalization and coupling.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior
datum with $s>0$, $f(r)=1-s/r$, exterior coordinate $x^0$, and stationary
field $T=\partial_0$. Let $0<\delta<s/2$ and put
$K_\delta:=\{(x^0,r,\omega):|r-3s/2|\leq\delta\}$ for $\omega\in S^2$.
Then $K_\delta$ is contained in $r>s$. On the static slice
$\Sigma_{x^0}:=\{x^0=\text{constant}\}$ the future unit normal is
$n=f^{-1/2}T$. For a smooth real test wave $\psi$ with finite initial
stationary energy, define

$$E_T[\psi](x^0):=\int_{\Sigma_{x^0}}Q_{ab}[\psi]n^aT^b\,d\mu_{\Sigma_{x^0}},\qquad E_{T,\delta}[\psi](x^0):=\int_{\Sigma_{x^0}\cap K_\delta}Q_{ab}[\psi]n^aT^b\,d\mu_{\Sigma_{x^0}}.$$

A **nondegenerate integrated local energy estimate with no trapping loss**
on $K_\delta$ means that there is a finite constant $C$, independent of
$\psi$, such that every smooth solution of $\Box_g\psi=0$ with finite
$E_T[\psi](0)$ satisfies

$$\int_0^\infty E_{T,\delta}[\psi](x^0)\,dx^0\leq C E_T[\psi](0).$$

Here “nondegenerate” means that the estimate integrates the full unweighted
first-derivative density, with no weight vanishing at $r=3s/2$; “no trapping
loss” means that the right side contains only the initial first-derivative
stationary energy, with no additional derivatives or degenerating weights.
This definition asserts no existence or nonexistence of such a constant.
Let $0<r<R$ and $n\ge 1$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:\mathbb R^n\to [0,1]$ such that $\rho=1$ on $\overline B_r(0)$ and $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq B_R(0)$.

derivations.claim:
Coordinates and angular functions. Put $r_0=3s/2$ and $x=r+s\log(r/s-1)-c$, with $c$ chosen so $x(r_0)=0$. Since $dx/dr=f^{-1}>0$ and the two endpoint limits are $-\infty,+\infty$, this is a smooth global radial coordinate with $r_x=f$. For an integer $l\ge1$ set $Y_l=c_l(\omega_1+i\omega_2)^l$, with the positive constant $c_l$ normalizing $\int_{S^2}|Y_l|^2=1$. This function is smooth at the poles by its polynomial expression. In polar coordinates it is $c_l\sin^l\vartheta\,e^{il\varphi}$; direct differentiation gives $\Delta_{S^2}Y_l=-l(l+1)Y_l$. Integration in $\varphi$ gives $\int Y_l^2=0$. Sphere integration by parts gives $\int|
abla Y_l|^2=l(l+1)$ and $\int
abla Y_l\cdot
abla Y_l=l(l+1)\int Y_l^2=0$. These identities can also be checked directly in the polar coordinates, where $\sin^l\vartheta$ removes the endpoint terms.

Exact scalar reduction. In $(t,x,\omega)$ the metric is $f(-dt^2+dx^2)+r^2\gamma_{S^2}$. Expanding $\Box_g$ in its volume density yields $\Box_g u=f^{-1}(-u_{tt}+r^{-2}\partial_x(r^2u_x))+r^{-2}\Delta_{S^2}u$. Substitution of $u=q(t,x)Y_l(\omega)/r(x)$ therefore gives precisely $q_{tt}-q_{xx}+W_lq=0$, with $W_l=f(l(l+1)/r^2+s/r^3)\ge0$. For each fixed $l$, $W_l$ and every $x$ derivative are bounded on $\mathbb R$: $\partial_x=f\partial_r$, the rational functions extend smoothly to $r=s$, and their derivatives decay at infinity. No uniform-in-$l$ bound is needed for existence.

Positive energy and real fields. For a compactly supported complex $q$ define $e_l[q]=\tfrac12\int_{\mathbb R}(|q_t|^2+|q_x|^2+W_l|q|^2)\,dx$. Use the sum of the real and imaginary scalar energies for a complex field. From [F2]--[F3], its energy density in $x,\omega$ is $\tfrac12(r^2|u_t|^2+r^2|u_x|^2+f|\nabla_{S^2}u|^2)$. For $qY_l/r$, integration over $S^2$ gives $\tfrac12(|q_t|^2+|q_x-bq|^2+fl(l+1)|q|^2/r^2)$, $b=f/r$. The identity $b'+b^2=fs/r^3$ and integration of $-b\partial_x|q|^2$, with zero endpoint terms, prove that its total energy equals $e_l[q]$. The zero bilinear angular integrals in step 1.1 give exactly $E_T[\operatorname{Re}(qY_l/r)]=e_l[q]/2$. The original local energy density is nonnegative on every radial subset. The factor $1/2$ for real fields also holds before the radial integration by parts, so no false boundary-term identity on a finite annulus is being used.

Global smooth radial Cauchy construction. For arbitrary compact smooth data $p,v$, solve the integral equation $q=q_0+\mathcal Kq$, where $q_0=(p(x+t)+p(x-t))/2+\tfrac12\int_{x-t}^{x+t}v(y)\,dy$ and $\mathcal Kq=-\tfrac12\int_0^t\int_{x-(t-a)}^{x+(t-a)}W_l(y)q(a,y)\,dy\,da$. On a slab of width $d$ its operator norm on bounded continuous functions is at most $\|W_l\|_\infty d^2/2$. Choose this below one. Picard iteration from $q_0$ then has geometrically summable successive sup-norm differences, so converges uniformly to the unique bounded continuous solution. Each iterate vanishes outside the unit-speed cone of the initial compact support. Spatial difference quotients of the integral equation inductively give continuous derivatives of every order: the highest differentiated unknown is acted on by the same $\mathcal K$, while all lower terms involve already known derivatives and bounded derivatives of $W_l$. Uniform convergence of these difference quotients follows from that same geometric estimate; the fundamental theorem of calculus identifies their limits as the derivatives. Differentiating the integral equation in time gives the initial velocity, $q_{tt}=q_{xx}-W_lq$, and all higher time derivatives. Thus the solution is jointly smooth. The fixed slab width depends on $l$ but not on the data size, so restart at successive endpoints and use uniqueness on overlaps to obtain a solution for every real time. Time reversal treats negative times. The iterates and their restarted solutions retain the compact unit-speed support cone. This is an actual Cauchy construction; global hyperbolicity or an unproved scalar-wave existence theorem has not been invoked.

Explicit Gaussian envelope. Let $h=(l+1/2)^{-1}$, $V_0=f/r^2$, $V_1=fs/r^3-V_0/4$. Then $W_l=h^{-2}V_0+V_1$. At $x=0$ direct differentiation gives $V_0(0)=\Omega^2$, $V_0'(0)=0$, $V_0''(0)/2=-\Omega^4$, where $\Omega=2/(3\sqrt3s)>0$. Indeed $\partial_rV_0=(-2r+3s)/r^4$, and $\partial_r^2V_0(r_0)=-3s/r_0^5$, with $\partial_x=f\partial_r$. Put $z(t)=\cosh(\Omega t)+i\sinh(\Omega t)$, $b(t)=\Omega^2(\cosh(\Omega t)-i\sinh(\Omega t))/z(t)$, and $a(t,y)=z(t)^{-1/2}e^{-b(t)y^2/2}$, using the smooth square-root branch equal to one initially. Since $\operatorname{Re}z>0$, it never vanishes. Calculation gives $\operatorname{Re}b=\Omega^2/|z|^2>0$, $b'=-i(b^2+\Omega^4)/\Omega$, and $(z^{-1/2})'/z^{-1/2}=-ib/(2\Omega)$. Therefore $2i\Omega a_t=-a_{yy}-\Omega^4y^2a$. On every fixed $|t|\le H$, all derivatives of $a$ are polynomials in $y$ with bounded coefficients times a Gaussian having $\operatorname{Re}b\ge c_H>0$; all required weighted $L^2$ norms are bounded uniformly there.

Frequency-independent energy stability. The same integral construction with an added d'Alembert forcing term treats smooth forcing on finite slabs. For a smooth spatially compact solution of $q_{tt}-q_{xx}+W_lq=F$, direct differentiation and integration by parts give $e_l'[q]=\operatorname{Re}\int F\overline{q_t}\,dx$. For nonzero $A=\|F\|_2$ and $B=\|q_t\|_2$, integration of $(|F|/A-|q_t|/B)^2\ge0$ gives $\int|Fq_t|\le AB$; zero-norm cases give the same inequality immediately. Since $W_l\ge0$, this bounds the energy derivative in absolute value by $\sqrt{2e_l[q]}\,\|F\|_2$. Apply this first to $\sqrt{e_l+\eta}$, integrate and let $\eta\downarrow0$ to obtain $\sqrt{e_l[q](t)}\le\sqrt{e_l[q](0)}+2^{-1/2}\int_0^t\|F(a)\|_2\,da$. In particular the energy of a homogeneous wave from step 3.2 is conserved. Compact support on every finite slab justifies all integrations, even though the full spatial line is noncompact.

Compact approximation and residual. Choose a real $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ from [F4], equal to one near $0$ and supported inside $\{|r(x)-r_0|<\delta\}$. Set $Q_h=h^{3/4}e^{-i\Omega t/h}\chi(x)a(t,x/\sqrt h)$. Its support and the support of each derivative lie in the exact annulus. In $R_h=(\partial_t^2-\partial_x^2+W_l)Q_h$, the $h^{-2}$ term cancels by $V_0(0)=\Omega^2$ and the $h^{-1}$ term cancels by the envelope equation in step 3.3. The remaining terms away from cutoff derivatives are $h^{3/4}e^{-i\Omega t/h}\chi$ times $a_{tt}+V_1a+h^{-2}(V_0(x)-\Omega^2+\Omega^4x^2)a$. Taylor's theorem on the fixed compact support bounds the last parenthesis by $C|x|^3$. With $dx=\sqrt h\,dy$, the amplitude prefactor changes an envelope $L^2$ norm by $h$. Thus the first two terms are $O_H(h)$ in $L^2_x$ and the cubic term is bounded by $Ch\,h^{-2}h^{3/2}\||y|^3a\|_2=O_H(\sqrt h)$. Cutoff commutators are $-2\chi'\partial_x$ of the uncut amplitude and $-\chi''$ times that amplitude. Their supports have $|x|\ge d_0>0$; Gaussian decay there makes their norms $O_{H,N}(h^N)$ for every $N$, despite any fixed derivative powers of $h^{-1}$. Consequently $\sup_{0\le t\le H}\|R_h(t)\|_2\le C_H\sqrt h$.

Positive normalization. At $t=0$, the substitution $x=\sqrt h\,y$ and Gaussian tail bounds show $e_l[Q_h](0)\to C_0=\Omega^2\int|a(0,y)|^2\,dy=\Omega\sqrt\pi>0$. More explicitly, the time derivative's leading term $-i\Omega Q_h/h$ contributes $\Omega^2\int|a_0|^2$ to the unhalved energy integral; $h^{-2}V_0|Q_h|^2$ contributes the same limit. Their cross/time-envelope terms are $O(h)$, the radial derivative energy is $O(h)$, and the $V_1$ term is $O(h^2)$. The factor $1/2$ in $e_l$ therefore gives $C_0+O(h)$. In particular this energy has a positive lower bound for sufficiently large integers $l$.

Exact correction. Use step 3.2 to solve the homogeneous radial equation with exactly the smooth compact initial data $Q_h(0),\partial_tQ_h(0)$, obtaining $q_h$ on all real times. Then $w_h=q_h-Q_h$ has zero initial data and forcing $-R_h$. Steps 4.1 and 4.2 give $\sup_{0\le t\le H}e_l[w_h](t)\le(H^2/2)\sup\|R_h(t)\|_2^2\le C_Hh$. Its compact support on finite slabs follows from the support of $q_h$ and $Q_h$. Define $U_h=\operatorname{Re}(q_hY_l/r)$. By steps 1.1--2.1 it is a real globally smooth exact scalar wave, including at the sphere poles, with compact smooth initial data. Its conserved stationary energy is exactly $e_l[Q_h](0)/2$ by steps 3.1 and 4.1.

Concentration on every required slice. Normalize $\psi_h=U_h/\sqrt{e_l[Q_h](0)/2}$; its stationary energy is exactly one on every slice. Outside $K_\delta$, the approximate field $\operatorname{Re}(Q_hY_l/r)$ and all its derivatives vanish. There the exact field equals the correction $\operatorname{Re}(w_hY_l/r)$. The original positive density of step 3.1 and the global energy identity consequently give $E_{T,\mathrm{outside}\ K_\delta}[\psi_h](t)\le e_l[w_h](t)/e_l[Q_h](0)\le C'_Hh$. The boundary spheres have measure zero, so total energy one implies $E_{T,\delta}[\psi_h](t)\ge1-C'_Hh$ simultaneously for all $t\in[0,H]$. Choose one sufficiently large integer $l$ with $C'_H/(l+1/2)<\epsilon$. This proves the exact quantifiers and real-field assertion. The construction uses the full specified radial annulus and makes no assertion about a smaller angular neighborhood or a frequency uniform in $H$.
